condition: Community-acquired pneumonia (high severity, CURB65 5) with sepsis
summary: 81-year-old woman with 2 days of cough and new confusion: RR 32, BP 86/54, HR 112, T 38.6, SpO₂ 90 %, urea 11.4. CURB65 5, qSOFA 3: hospital/critical-care assessment, blood cultures and IV antibiotics within 1 hour.

inputs.hpi: Brought by her daughter: two days of cough with rusty sputum and fevers, today muddled and not recognising the grandchildren. Not eating. Attends our clinic for surveillance after a sigmoid colectomy.

exam.general: Drowsy but rousable, confused (AMT 6/10), dry mucous membranes.
exam.respiratory: Bronchial breathing and coarse crackles left base, RR 32.

confirmedDiagnosis.name: Severe community-acquired pneumonia with sepsis
confirmedDiagnosis.assessmentText: Left basal pneumonia, CURB65 5, with sepsis and hypotension: sepsis bundle, IV antibiotics within 1 hour, critical-care review.

values.note: RR 32, SBP 86 and AVPU C are all on the record; auto-fill reads vitals.

mustInclude.proposedFix: Protocols for the PANE nodes pneumonia and sepsis (BTS CAP / NICE NG51: blood cultures before antibiotics), or a sepsis prompt that adds blood cultures as an investigation.

guideline.name: NICE NG250 - Pneumonia: diagnosis and management
guideline.section: Community-acquired pneumonia: severity assessment with clinical judgement and CRB65 (community) / CURB65 (hospital); low severity managed in the community with oral amoxicillin; higher severity: hospital assessment, microbiology, antibiotics within 4 hours of presentation (1 hour if sepsis suspected)
guideline.citation: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence. Pneumonia: diagnosis and management (NG250). London: NICE; 2025 (replaces CG191 and NG138).

guideline.name: BTS guidelines for the management of community acquired pneumonia in adults: update 2009
guideline.section: Severity assessment: CURB65 (confusion; urea >7 mmol/L; RR >=30/min; SBP <90 or DBP <=60 mmHg; age >=65); 0-1 low severity (home), 2 moderate (consider hospital), 3-5 high severity (hospital, assess for critical care); blood cultures for moderate and high severity
guideline.citation: Lim WS, Baudouin SV, George RC, et al. Thorax. 2009;64(Suppl 3):iii1-55.

guideline.name: Surviving Sepsis Campaign: international guidelines for management of sepsis and septic shock 2021
guideline.section: Screening: recommend against qSOFA alone compared with SIRS, NEWS or MEWS; antimicrobials within 1 h for possible septic shock or high likelihood of sepsis; blood cultures before antimicrobials; lactate measurement; 30 mL/kg IV crystalloid within 3 h for sepsis-induced hypoperfusion or septic shock; noradrenaline first-line vasopressor, MAP target 65 mmHg
guideline.citation: Evans L, Rhodes A, Alhazzani W, et al. Crit Care Med. 2021;49:e1063-e1143.

guideline.name: NICE NG51 - Suspected sepsis: recognition, diagnosis and early management
guideline.section: Think sepsis in anyone with a possible infection, including people who are afebrile, older or frail; NEWS2 used for risk stratification in adults in acute hospital settings; high risk -> senior review, blood cultures, lactate and antibiotics within 1 hour
guideline.citation: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence. NG51. London: NICE; 2016 (updated 2024).

guideline.name: Third International Consensus Definitions for Sepsis and Septic Shock (Sepsis-3)
guideline.section: qSOFA: respiratory rate >=22/min, altered mentation, systolic BP <=100 mmHg; >=2 identifies infected patients at risk of poor outcome outside the ICU
guideline.citation: Singer M, Deutschman CS, Seymour CW, et al. JAMA. 2016;315:801-10.

guideline.name: Royal College of Physicians - National Early Warning Score (NEWS) 2
guideline.section: Clinical response thresholds: aggregate 5-6 or a single parameter scoring 3 -> urgent response; aggregate >=7 -> emergency response; SpO2 Scale 2 only for confirmed hypercapnic respiratory failure
guideline.citation: Royal College of Physicians. National Early Warning Score (NEWS) 2: standardising the assessment of acute-illness severity in the NHS. London: RCP; 2017.

guideline.name: BTS guideline for oxygen use in healthcare and emergency settings
guideline.section: Target SpO2 94-98% for most acutely ill patients; 88-92% for patients at risk of hypercapnic respiratory failure (e.g. COPD) pending blood gases
guideline.citation: O'Driscoll BR, Howard LS, Earis J, Mak V. Thorax. 2017;72(Suppl 1):ii1-90.

rationale: High-severity permutation: CURB65 5 (confusion, urea >7, RR >=30, SBP <90, age >=65) with septic shock physiology. Every engine should escalate to emergency.
